key_insight: An equivalent-circuit model links a reverse diode to inefficient electron extraction and S-shaped current–voltage behavior in valley photovoltaic devices.
engineering_relevance: Eliminating the reverse-diode behavior is a prerequisite for high-efficiency valley photovoltaic devices.
method: Measure intensity- and voltage-dependent photoluminescence and electrical responses.
Model both responses with a shared equivalent circuit.
Use Poisson/drift-diffusion simulations to investigate reverse-diode origins.
evidence_signal: The equivalent circuit captures the measured S-shaped current–voltage curves while simultaneously describing photoluminescence and electrical measurements.
watch_item: Simulations identify valley scattering and a heterojunction barrier as possible origins, but the abstract does not establish which dominates or demonstrate a remedy.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
